ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014, Law No. 8 of 2016, and Law No. 154 of 2018, and the Executive Regulations issued by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE); Cabinet Decree No. 164 of 2019 concerning customer due diligence and ultimate beneficial owner identification; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (the Unified Companies Law) and its Executive Regulations; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI regulations on commercial registration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / national civil registry of the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (Egypt is a contracting party since 2022); for non-apostille countries, consular legalization at the Egyptian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Essence du Contrat) and draft LLC incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Local Notarial Authority in Egypt (for the notarized deed) and competent authority in the foreign UBO's country for cross-border signature verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation of the general commercial registry abstract or equivalent foreign registration document of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered or supervised foreign Companies Registry / Chamber of Commerce in the corporate shareholder's state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by certification by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs or GAFI for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Physical Registered Office Address (lease contract or title deed) endorsed for use in the legal entity's commercial registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Real Estate Registration Authority / Notary Public in Egypt; if leased by a foreign UBO, the foreign lease or ownership document must be legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: No-Objection Certificate or preliminary health compliance clearance for the retail of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Health and Population – Central Administration for Pharmaceutical Affairs (or relevant district health directorate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certification with notarization; no apostille required unless used outside Egypt

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial shareholders against the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list, the EU/UK HM Treasury consolidated financial sanctions list, the Central Bank of Egypt's domestic terrorism lists, and the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit (MLCU) circulars. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) and transaction monitoring are required for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates, in accordance with the CBE's AML/CFT rules and Egypt's National Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Strategy. Additional sanctions screening is mandated for cross-border e-commerce payment flows under CBE Resolution No. 4800 of 1996 as amended, requiring risk-based confirmation of customer identity and location.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Online Services Portal and Egyptian Commercial Registry System (www.gafi.gov.eg; www.investinegypt.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in Arabic. A Latin transliteration or French/English transliteration may appear as a commercial/brand name, but the registered legal name in the Commercial Registry and notarized Articles of Association must expressly match the Arabic name. Transliteration rules follow Egyptian Civil Registration and General Notary Board protocols. The name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Egyptian registered entity, foreign trademark registered in Egypt, or an internationally recognized mark with local goodwill.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: International (when used to imply governmental authority or territorial scope)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, a written appeal must be submitted to the GAFI Commercial Registration Department within 15 days of the rejection notification, stating the grounds and proposed mitigation. If the administrative appeal is denied or not answered within 30 days, the applicant may file a petition with the Administrative Court in Cairo within 60 days of the final rejection decision. A name reservation can be renewed for further 30-day periods only where the initial commercial registration process is already pending before GAFI, not as of right beyond two renewals in non-contentious circumstances.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not Permissible for this high-risk cross-border dietary supplements retail business. A virtual office may be acceptable for pure consulting or non-licensed trading activities, but the e-commerce supply of nutraceuticals and dietary supplements triggers mandatory physical premises under law, including a dedicated operational site with temperature-controlled storage, a customer complaint/return area, and a registered manager present at the commercial address. GAFI and the Ministry of Health will not accept a virtual address or serviced mailbox alone.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High Risk Quantified: 72% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by GAFI, the Ministry of Health and Population, or the Consumer Protection Agency within the first 12 months of commercial registration, primarily to verify physical storage, packaging labels, safe handling, and the presence of the responsible pharmacist/health compliance officer.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 5 of 2015, particularly Articles 102, 106, and 110 governing LLCs; Executive Regulations No. 96 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, Cairo One-Stop-Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Notice (Ikhbar Al-Ta'sis) and Notarized Constitutive Contract (Aqed El-Ta'sis)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under Companies Law No. 159/1981. The constitutive contract fixes the capital, which must be fully subscribed and at least 50% paid-up before filing. Paid-in funds must be deposited in an Egyptian bank and evidenced by a bank certificate submitted to GAFI. For e-commerce supplement distribution, the Commercial Licensing Authority may require a minimum paid-up capital of EGP 500,000 as a market-entry condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscribers herein, being the initial members of EG_LLC, hereby approve and adopt the Constitutive Contract and Articles of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the capital as stated therein is duly subscribed, and the undersigned founders irrevocably designate the registered office located in Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt, as the Company's principal place of business. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the appointed Managers are each authorized to manage ordinary operations, open bank accounts, bind the Company, and execute e-commerce, merchant acquiring, and supply agreements. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the Secretary be instructed to complete all statutory filings, publish the incorporation notice, and obtain all operational licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Integrated Services Center (Tasmeem) – online portal and Cairo One-Stop-Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three Arabic and English proposed company names through the GAFI electronic reservation module. The system conducts a word-for-word collision check against the commercial register. Pay the non-refundable name reservation fee via e-payment. Obtain the official Name Reservation Certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Copy of valid passports of all founding individuals or entity authorization
Business activity description (ISIC 4791 – online retail of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals)
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is denied due to similarity or prohibited expression, file an administrative objection with the GAFI Name Committee within 15 days and concurrently resubmit two alternative names to preserve the timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Conststitutive Contract and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Authority (Tawthiq) – General Notary Office competent for the registered office location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Constitutive Contract and Articles of Association in Arabic, signed in person or by attorney-in-fact by all founding members. Appear before the notary with valid identification and the name reservation certificate. The notary verifies the legal capacity of the signatories and formalizes the corporate contract. Retain the notarized original for GAFI filing.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Draft Constitutive Contract and Articles of Association (Arabic)
Valid passports or national ID cards of all founding members
Power of attorney if a representative signs
Proposed registered office address (lease or proof of ownership)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires corrections, obtain a signed addendum/rectification from all members and re-notarize the same instrument; no new name reservation is needed unless the legal name changes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Paid-Up Capital Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate bank account in the name of the company being formed. Deposit the paid-up portion of the share capital and obtain a capital deposit certificate indicating account-holder name, account number, and balance. The bank will confirm that the funds are frozen until GAFI incorporation certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Notarized Constitutive Contract and initial board resolution
Name reservation certificate
Passports or national IDs of authorized signatories
Proof of registered office address
Tax registration form (preliminary if available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays the certificate based on know-your-customer deficiencies, supplement the file with a notarized declaration of ultimate beneficial owners and government-issued utility bill; escalate to the CBE complaints unit if clearance exceeds 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing with GAFI and Issuance of Establishment Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application package to GAFI electronically or in person at the Cairo One-Stop-Shop. GAFI reviews the impermissibility of the activity, legality of the constitutive contract, and completeness of dossiers. After substantive check, GAFI issues the Establishment Certificate (Shahadat Qayd) which constitutes legal personality and commercial registration enablement.
required_dossiers: Notarized Constitutive Contract and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Name reservation certificate
Identities and addresses of founders and managers
Rental contract or title deed of registered office
Statement of activities including ISIC 4791 and nutraceutical e-commerce description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a technical query or 'temporary rejection', respond in writing within the 30-day cure period. Amend the constitutive contract and re-notarize if requested. If the decision is unlawful, appeal before the GAFI Administrative Grievance Committee and subsequently the Economic Courts within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Commercial Registry, and Post-Incorporation License Pathway
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry; Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Establishment Certificate, register the company with ETA for tax card and VAT. Complete commercial registration with the Commercial Registry, which issues the Commercial Registry Certificate and a unique commercial registration number. Concurrently, pre-file the license application with EDA for the retail of food supplements and an online store commercial license from the competent Supply Administration.
required_dossiers: GAFI Establishment Certificate
Constitutive Contract and board resolution on officer appointments
Valid passports and residential proofs of managers
Proof of registered office and warehouse/storage address
Procedural tax forms and VAT registration application
Bank account details
Draft store policy, anti-counterfeit, product storage and traceability plan for supplement retail
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA or Commercial Registry rejects the application, determine the specific deficiency, resubmit within 15 days. For EDA licensing delay, request a provisional operation permit pending inspection; engage an expedited compliance audit to address product registration and storage requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) – Sector for Medical Nutrition and Food Supplements Licensing; Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade – Commercial Licensing Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment Operating License for Retail of Food Supplements and Nutraceuticals via Electronic Commerce

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Environmental Compliance and Inspection Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Limited Environmental Impact Registration (as an e-commerce distribution and non-manufacturing fulfillment operation)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: no chemical manufacturing discharge; wastewater discharge must meet Law 4/1994 and Ministerial Decree 44/2000 limits; VOC emissions negligible due to no production process; packaging waste must be segregated and recycled in accordance with the Waste Management Law No. 202/2020; storage areas must maintain temperature conditions per product indication and implement spill containment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Life Safety Certification from the Civil Defense Authority (General Administration of Civil Defense) for the registered office, storage facility, and fulfillment center; structural load inspection certificate for shelving and palletized storage; occupational health and workplace safety clearance under Labor Law No. 12/2003, including fire suppression, emergency exits, first aid, and defined storage area ventilation requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt; official electronic portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg (unified taxpayer registry, CIT/VAT filing, and e-invoicing/e-receipts fiscal clearance gateway).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested Egyptian LLC obtains its statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and unified tax card by: (1) completing incorporation with the Commercial Registry (Al-Sijil Al-Tijari) and, where foreign shareholding applies, the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); (2) submitting to the ETA the certificate of incorporation, certified articles of association, commercial registry extract, registered-office lease, and designation of the general manager or local tax representative; (3) applying separately for VAT registration under Law 67/2016 once annual taxable supplies reach or are reasonably expected to exceed EGP 500,000, with voluntary registration permitted below that threshold; (4) obtaining an electronic signature certificate and activating ETA e-portal credentials for CIT, VAT, withholding, and e-invoice transmission; and (5) for card-acquiring e-commerce merchants, presenting the payment-licence evidence to the ETA so that the taxpayer's profile is correctly flagged for e-invoicing and e-receipt obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Egyptian system does not provide check-the-box pass-through or hybrid-mismatch transparency elections; the LLC is an opaque resident corporation taxed under Law 91/2005 at the standard CIT rate of 22.5%. Available statutory elections include: (i) an accounting fiscal-year-end election requiring ETA pre-approval; (ii) the small- and medium-enterprise presumptive revenue-based tax regime under Law 6/2018 for eligible enterprises below the statutory turnover ceiling; (iii) the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) investment election under Law 83/2002, which permits qualifying export-oriented licensees to obtain a 0% CIT/privileged fiscal treatment certificate; and (iv) an accrual-basis versus cash-basis election for VAT may be available to small registered taxpayers under the ETA executive regulations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Egyptian VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 (replacing the former General Sales Tax Law No. 11/1991)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods and services constitutes the mandatory VAT registration trigger under Law 67/2016 and its executive regulations; registration is optional below this economic turnover threshold, and a non-resident supplier selling to Egyptian consumers may be required to appoint a fiscal representative where Egyptian-source supplies arise.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A compulsory real-time fiscal clearance regime applies: the LLC must issue all sales invoices in ETA-approved XML/JSON format, transmit them through the ETA e-invoicing platform via direct API or a licensed service provider, and obtain a unique digital UUID and QR-code stamping before the invoice becomes legally valid for input VAT deduction. E-receipts are separately mandated for point-of-sale and online B2C transactions. Invoices not cleared in real time are rejected by the system, attract statutory fines, and cannot sustain an input VAT credit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to (i) dietary-supplement goods physically exported from Egypt and discharged under a definitive NAFEZA-automated customs export declaration; (ii) services rendered to non-resident customers for use wholly outside Egypt where the direct benefit is located abroad; and (iii) internationally related transport services, provided in each case that the consideration is paid in freely convertible foreign currency and the export proceeds are received in Egypt within the mandatory repatriation window. The exporter must evidence a genuine non-resident buyer, enforceable sales contract, actual cross-border movement, and proper e-invoicing with the 0% export code so that underlying input VAT on raw materials and fulfilment costs remains creditable and refundable from the ETA.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (El-Bayane El-Goomrukee) signed by the licensed clearing agent and matched to the NAFEZA single-window release record
Commercial invoice (final/definitive) stating the foreign-currency export value and the 0% VAT code
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical dispatch from Egyptian customs territory to the non-resident buyer
Signed purchase order or export contract reflecting terms of sale, Incoterms, and payment of convertible currency
Foreign-exchange inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds into an Egyptian bank account
Certificate of origin and, where applicable, Egyptian Drug Authority supplementary clearance records for the nutraceutical product
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA reconciles zero-rated export claims against customs export declarations, bank FX records, and e-invoice clearances. Where export zero-rating is found to be unsupported, fictitious, or inflated, the ETA reverts the supply to the 14% standard VAT rate, disallows and claws back associated input VAT credits, and imposes the statutory default increment of 2% per month on the outstanding tax, together with civil penalty multipliers applicable to tax evasion. Proven fraudulent export invoicing or forged customs/FX documentation carries criminal exposure under the VAT Law, including fines linked to the evaded tax and imprisonment of the responsible directors or tax representatives, while the Central Bank of Egypt may additionally suspend export clearance privileges and initiate sanctions for unrepatriated foreign-exchange proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt applies current-account convertibility for trade, services and investment income under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194/2020, but foreign-currency flows must pass through authorized banks and be supported by underlying contracts, corporate documents and CBE declarations. Capital-account transactions such as equity injections, shareholder loans and intra-group financings are not freely convertible and must be documented for CBE/GAFI registration. Profit remittance to a foreign shareholder is lawful, but the remitting bank will require current audited financial statements, proof of dividend approval and payment of Egyptian corporate and withholding taxes, an inward remittance trail for the original foreign capital, and a bank-completed CBE transfer/undertaking form. The practical hurdles are not the formal exchange-control license but bank-level KYC, source-of-funds reconciliation and foreign-currency liquidity on the interbank market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE exchange-control rules, export proceeds must be repatriated to a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank within 180 calendar days from the date of shipment, normally evidenced by bill of lading/airwaybill. The proceeds must be credited to the exporter's foreign-currency account and the exporter must execute the standard export-proceeds surrender undertaking. The default mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of export proceeds into EGP at the bank's prevailing interbank rate, subject to any CBE-approved foreign-currency retention quota, which in current practice may allow up to 50% of proceeds to be retained for verified import payments for the LLC's own trade operations. A new LLC without an approved retention facility should plan on 100% surrender and conversion. Non-compliance may trigger CBE fines, denial of trade facilities and referral to the Egyptian AML/authorization enforcement regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EGP and USD current account with dedicated export-proceeds sub-account; capital escrow account can be opened if shareholder injections require escrow
Operational EGP and FX current accounts plus ACI/import letter-of-credit clearing account
Treasury settlement account and trade-finance operational account for FX forwards, swaps and documentary credits
Operational EGP/FX account and high-risk merchant settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for an offshore EMI/neobank as the primary treasury rail; MEDIUM only as an ancillary offshore collection node if all funds ultimately land in a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank account. Offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex, Paysera or white-label neobanks cannot lawfully hold EGP, clear EGP, or operate as local banks in Egypt unless licensed by the CBE under Law 194/2020 and the payment system regulation. Using such EMIs as the principal account creates a KYC/AML blocker because the bank cannot verify the ultimate source of funds and the exchange control repatriation route is broken. A compliant structure is to use CBE-licensed fintech acquirers or PSPs in Egypt, such as Paymob or Fawry for local card acquiring, with daily settlement into the onshore NBE or Banque Misr operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required in practice for a non-resident-owned high-risk LLC. CBE AML/CFT rules do not expressly ban remote open banking, but underwriting standards for cross-border nutraceutical e-commerce will impose an in-person interview in Cairo by the bank compliance officer with the Egyptian legal representative, the local manager and at least one authorized signatory/UBO. Foreign directors may use a notarized Arabic power of attorney legalized through an Egyptian consulate, but the bank will still require the company's commercial registration extract, tax card, translated and legalized corporate documents, UBO declarations and a local meeting at the branch before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with no recognizable Egyptian economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum/Articles of Association, CBE-format register of UBOs, board minutes appointing Egyptian manager, Commercial Registration extract from GAFI, Cairo office or warehouse lease, local payroll records, tax card and notarized POA from foreign directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nutraceutical/pharma product flagged as high-risk health claim or unlicensed medical product
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) or Ministry of Health import/product registration, free-sale certificate from country of origin, Good Manufacturing Practice certificate, ISO 22000 or HACCP certification, product composition/safety data sheet, Arabic labeling compliance proof and evidence that no controlled prescription ingredients are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk web business with elevated credit-card chargeback and refund exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE-licensed acquiring agreement or PSP letter, 12-month transaction and chargeback forecast, refund and dispute policy, PCI DSS certificate, product liability insurance, order-management system audit trail, and logistics contracts proving physical delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for capital injection and shareholder loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement from shareholder's home institution, audited financial statements of the beneficial owner, signed share subscription agreement, source-of-wealth tax return, CBE inward remittance declaration, board resolution authorizing the transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP and reputation exposure of directors/UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passports, proof of residential address, World-Check/Oracle sanctions and PEP screening reports, notarized non-PEP declarations, police clearance/certificates of good conduct, and corporate group structure chart showing no sanctioned jurisdiction connection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border sales into high-risk or unrestricted end-consumer markets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance-approved export market list, restricted-party screening log, end-customer due diligence for B2B wholesale buyers, sanctions compliance manual, certificates of origin and export declarations, and product safety/regulatory certificates for each destination.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder's equity or working-capital loan must be sent by SWIFT MT103 from an account in the shareholder's own name to the EG LLC's account at a CBE-licensed bank. The wire must use the correct CBE balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment in Egypt or intercompany capital inflow, and the payment reference must include the company Commercial Registration number and Tax Card number. The receiving bank will require the board resolution, subscription schedule and inward-remittance declaration, then issue an inward remittance certificate and register the capital in CBE systems. Cash deposits, third-party digital wallet transfers and unregulated foreign-account transfers are not accepted; non-cash contributions require GAFI/valuation/import documentation and cannot be cleared as bank capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imports of pharmaceutical and nutraceutical finished goods or raw materials, the LLC should use either a direct SWIFT MT103 payment or an irrevocable documentary letter of credit. The compliant sequence is: obtain the supplier proforma invoice and contract; confirm the goods have the Egyptian Drug Authority import approval and ACI advanced cargo information via CargoX/NAFEZA; instruct the Egyptian bank to issue an at-sight commercial LC in USD/EUR/CNY; and pay on presentation of invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airwaybill, certificate of analysis and certificate of origin. For smaller low-risk suppliers, an MT103 after customs clearance is acceptable. Each outbound wire requires correct SWIFT/BIC/IBAN, trade settlement purpose code and proof of the underlying commercial transaction; payments to sanctioned jurisdictions or unlicensed intermediaries are blocked.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP and EUR/EGP FX forward contracts with tenors capped at 180 days and strictly backed by genuine import/export invoices or awarded trade contracts
FX swaps and rollover facilities to bridge timing mismatches between export USD receipts and USD/EUR import payments, executed through a CBE-licensed bank trade-finance line
Cross-currency interest-rate and principal swaps for qualifying medium-term trade loans, subject to CBE derivative documentation and underlying loan approval
Shariah-compliant FX promises or Wa'd arrangements offered by Islamic banks for genuine trade risk coverage, but speculative/uncovered positions are not permitted

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the Egyptian pound are not a permissible onshore hedge for a domestic LLC and should not be booked through the Egyptian banking system; the LLC should rely only on CBE-regulated deliverable products

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal Declaration (Tajdeed Al-Sijill Al-Tijari)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing during January of each year; deadline 31 January for all registered businesses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts late-restoration fines under Law 34/1976; non-renewal for one full calendar year provides the basis for administrative strike-off and loss of the commercial registration number.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for Legal Persons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months from fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer the return is due by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to monthly late-payment penalty on unpaid tax (statutory rate from date of default), late-filing fines up to EGP 100,000 under Law 91/2005, and continued non-compliance triggers collection enforcement, asset attachment, and civil remedies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Audited Financial Statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes, cash flow statement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and shareholders of the LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus five months for tax submission; shareholders' approval and audited accounts must be completed within six months of the LLC's financial period closing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited accounts invalidates the annual tax filing and permits the ETA to impose turnover-based tax assessments; repeated non-deposit with the company records constitutes a corporate governance breach under Law 159/1981.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statement of Registered Address, Managers and Shareholding Schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Co-filed with the commercial registry renewal; due by 31 January for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or inaccurate filing exposes the managers to personal liability under the Companies Law; persistent failure to keep the registry current will result in dishonoring of corporate acts and potential adverse administrative measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian limited liability companies, regardless of size or turnover, are obliged to appoint at least one certified public external auditor under Law 159/1981; there is no statutory turnover-based exemption for LLCs. Additionally, the Egyptian Tax Authority requires audited financial statements with the annual tax return whenever the company exceeds the bookkeeping thresholds set by Law 91/2005.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by the Ministry of Investment, which are substantially aligned with IFRS; IFRS is permissible for entities with foreign listing or where required by parent reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egypt maintains a beneficial-owner register for LLCs. No standalone annual UBO return is required; however, the register must be updated within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership. At the time of annual commercial registry renewal, the LLC must confirm to GAFI that the existing UBO register remains current and has no unexplained transfers; any transfer of membership interests must be recorded in the LLC's members register and submitted with the annual corporate declaration to the Commercial Registry.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Zone projects are exempt from CIT for 50 years on export profits; Investment Law No. 72/2017 qualifying projects may benefit from a 50% CIT reduction on taxable profits for up to 5 years; additional investment cost deductions of 30%–50% apply to eligible fixed capital expenditures; SME simplified regimes in the 0.25%–1% gross-receipts range are available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Corporate Tax Return) – Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Electronic Filing Portal (e-Tax Authority)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with four equal advance quarterly installments during the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual self-assessment return must be filed within four months after the close of the corporate fiscal year; final CIT payment falls due on the filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales / operating revenue from online nutraceutical sales; excluding VAT and returns; includes all Egyptian-source e-commerce revenue attributable to the contractual supply chain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident LLC must report only revenue effectively connected with an Egyptian permanent establishment, and attach a revenue-allocation statement excluding offshore fulfillment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: freight, customs duties, procurement, and direct storage costs for dietary supplements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use arm's-length transfer prices substantiated by contemporaneous TP documentation; do not inflate costs with head-office service charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before tax adjustments, prepared in accordance with Egyptian Accounting Standards or IFRS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the Egyptian branch's commercial accounts to the head-office accounts and disclose all intercompany allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-back of disallowed provisions, excessive depreciation, entertainment expenses, and related-party charges that fail the arm's-length or substance test.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back head-office management fees and royalties that lack economic substance or correspond to no actual service; document beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income net of loss carryforward and investment incentives; compute final CIT, deduct prepayments and foreign tax credits, and show the net payable or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty relief only if the non-resident establishes residency via a valid Tax Residency Certificate and is the beneficial owner of the income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: statutory fine of EGP 5,000 – EGP 20,000 per return; late payment: monthly delay surcharge of 1% of unpaid tax for each month or fraction of a month, plus a potential 20% deficiency penalty if the final assessment exceeds the self-assessed liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid to non-residents, unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty (often 0%–5% for substantial shareholdings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA, the non-resident recipient must obtain an annual Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, have it apostilled or legalized and translated into Arabic, and submit it to the ETA along with an ETA relief application Form before distribution. The Egyptian paying entity may withhold at the treaty rate after ETA pre-approval; if excessive tax is withheld, the recipient must file a refund claim through the ETA International Taxation Unit, supplementing the TRC with beneficial-ownership and economic-substance evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for intellectual property: statutory WHT 20%; treaty rates typically 10%–15% if the recipient is beneficial owner. Interest on cross-border loans: statutory WHT 20%; treaty rates typically 10%–15%. Jumbo contracts split into 'service' and 'IP' components are re-characterized wholly as royalties if the dominant purpose is royalty avoidance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the aggregate annual value of related-party transactions exceeds EGP 10 million; Master File is required where the Egyptian entity belongs to a group with consolidated global turnover above EGP 3 billion or related-party transactions above EGP 300 million; CbC reporting threshold aligns with OECD EUR 750 million consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulation. Nonetheless, the ETA applies the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR introduced by Law No. 211/2020), substance-over-form jurisprudence, beneficial-ownership requirements under tax treaties, and Central Bank AML licensing/KYC standards. A letterbox LLC lacking premises, employees, and operational control in Egypt will be re-characterized as a dummy vehicle and may lose treaty, free zone, and investment-law incentives.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of online supplement sales, use of inflated inbound invoices from an affiliated foreign supplier, omission of Egyptian-source e-commerce income generated through local logistic hubs, or forging VAT/tax registration documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years, criminal fine of 25%–100% of the evaded tax, confiscation of goods and funds, full recovery of unpaid tax plus the monthly 1% delay surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign or cause false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and may be subject to criminal prosecution, travel bans, asset attachment, and disqualification from board service; the LLC veil is pierced where the director is the actual controller of the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a shell LLC with no physical office in Egypt, no employees, no local management, and automated drop-shipping of nutraceuticals sourced abroad, while claiming treaty benefits or Investment Law incentives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive denial of Investment Law 72/2017 tax holidays and free-zone exemptions; re-characterization of the entity as non-existent for tax purposes with reassessment and penalties; deregistration of the company; fine for false declarations up to EGP 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for unpaid tax and third-party e-commerce refunds; non-resident directors may be banned from entering Egypt and subject to contempt orders until final judgment is satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and file the Local File/Master File when related-party transaction values exceed the EGP 10 million / EGP 300 million thresholds, or fabrication of CUP/Resale Price calculations to shift profits to a Cayman or Hong Kong intercompany distributor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP audit adjustment increasing Egyptian taxable income, plus a monthly 1% delay surcharge on the additional tax; an additional fine of up to 100% of the tax difference for fraudulent documentation; ETA may impose a penalty of 5% of the value of undocumented controlled transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve TP policies can be named as jointly liable for the TP adjustment; ETA referral to the Public Prosecutor may lead to criminal sanctions for intentional under-declaration and personal seizure of offshore assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating under a high-risk nutraceuticals e-commerce license without a registered AML compliance officer, failing KYC/CDD for merchant customers, processing layering transactions through unlicensed 'P2P' intermediaries, or underreporting credit-card settlements to finance cross-border structured purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80/2002, imprisonment up to 7 years, fine ranging between EGP 10,000 and EGP 1,000,000 per offense, freezing of Egyptian bank and merchant accounts, revocation of the commercial license, and confiscation of assets linked to laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are personally prosecutable; additional penalties include deportation (if non-resident), travel bans, direct personal attachment of funds, and being barred from serving in any Egyptian commercial entity.
